name: Answer Highlight
description: A question, an answer that writes itself a word at a time, then a caret lands mid-sentence and drags a selection across the one statement that matters — and settles onto one word inside it

name: Agent Steps
description: An agent narrating its own work — a log that writes itself one line at a time, always on the centre line, then swells and clears until only the answer is left

name: Announce Title
description: A four-shot launch title — the eyebrow rushes past the camera on a receding type plane, the name assembles on paper, and a macro pan cuts wide as the tagline builds itself last word first

name: Answer Stream
description: The beat after send — a macro shot on the button cuts hard to the answer building itself, while the camera pulls back about a focal point above the frame to keep up with it

name: Text Reveal
description: A cinematic zoom-out title reveal — the lead word appears large, then scales down and slides into place as the sentence sweeps in and settles

name: Text Highlight
description: Animated emphasis on one span inside a static sentence — marker, color, underline, strikethrough, or shimmer

name: Text Rewrite
description: A line writes itself, is selected, then has its opening swept away by a clip that cuts letters in half — and a new ending written on while it slides to its new centre

name: Text Select
description: A line that writes itself a word at a time — each arriving in the accent and cooling a beat later, so one word is ever coloured — then pushes forward to full size and gets selected under a shining gradient

name: Text Swap
description: Replace one line of text with another using exit-then-enter scheduling and five transition presets

name: Text Swell
description: The lead word floats toward you and hangs there while the sentence assembles around it, letters bouncing up off the baseline — then the whole line falls back

name: Text Build
description: Words enter one at a time while the already-placed words reflow to stay centered — as a line or a stack

name: Word Flip
description: A headline types itself out, then one word cycles on a 3D flip — anticipation dip, motion-blurred throw, zero reflow

name: Word Captions
description: Burned-in captions in the styles big channels use — the YouTube box by default (white Roboto on a per-line black box), plus outlined and accent presets

name: Karaoke Captions
description: A caption line over any footage — the YouTube per-line black box by default, with karaoke fill, highlight-bar, and pill presets

name: Logo Drift
description: A field of stack tiles drifting past a headline while the camera pulls steadily back, so the wall of things-it-works-with keeps arriving from every edge

name: Logo Assemble
description: A ring of image cards revolves and drains to the centre, giving birth to a simple logo that slides left as the brand name reveals to its right

name: Logo Flicker
description: Images flip across the screen very fast, the flicker decelerates and fades, and the logo and brand name resolve underneath

name: Block Wordmark
description: A square scales in, a deck of coloured cards fans out around it and winds back, then the stack stretches into one block per letter and each block flashes a colour and swaps for its real letterform

name: Phone Frame
description: iPhone-style device frame with a dynamic island — sways in 3D showing off a glowing ride-summary map that draws itself

name: Laptop Frame
description: MacBook that opens, runs a notch notification, then dives into the screen until an image or video fills the frame

name: Terminal Simulator
description: Terminal window with chunked command playback, freeze-frame pauses, step scrolling, and an optional cursor-pinned zoom

name: Screen Recording
description: Crops the browser and OS chrome off a raw screen capture, fits what is left to the frame, and runs a keyframed camera that pushes in on whatever matters

name: Count Grid
description: A grid of cards rushes in under a horizontal smear and settles on five, then the camera pulls back a fraction while every empty cell fills in from the middle out and the count jumps from five to five hundred

name: Roster Grant
description: Three rows of roster cards stream past a call to action, a pointer walks in and clicks it, and the monograms start turning to the accent one every seven frames — top, middle, bottom, top, bottom, middle

name: Wordmark Cut
description: A wordmark twice the width of the frame, cooling from a lit gradient to ink as it settles, then a hard cut onto its last letters and the dot — nearer, shallower, and pushing in

name: Cursor Track
description: A synthetic cursor that walks a path of waypoints over any children and pulses a click ring on arrival — for sims, and for recordings whose cursor never made the file

name: Follower Rush
description: An X-style follower notification that piles up — avatars stack in and the count explodes, then the row bends into an undulating wave of faces

name: Prompt Send
description: A composer that unrolls from a hairline, writes a brief while the camera cuts in and rides the caret, then cuts back out as a pointer arrives and sends it — with typing that eases in and out instead of ticking

name: Prompt Mark
description: A prompt types into a pill, the camera pans to send, the arrow becomes the snapcn mark and a bloom flashes it into a logo lockup

name: Prompt Zoom
description: An assistant landing screen that offers its suggestions, then cuts hard into the caret — a measured 2.547× push anchored on the text insertion point — where the prompt types itself

name: Punch Lines
description: Full-frame title cards that cut hard between beats — a statement flicked in line by line and rushed past the camera, then a hero line whose words punch up from a third of their size

name: Orbit Gallery
description: A ring of feature cards orbits a central product mark, each rotating upright as it swings to the front

name: Product Hero
description: Cinematic product-launch hero — two cards slide into formation as the headline reveals above

name: Moodboard Reveal
description: A kinetic headline with a swapping inline image, then a scattered photo gallery flies in and the camera pushes through it — dark to light — onto a hero image

name: Reel Collage
description: A photo reel between two captions shuts like an eyelid, the captions fold into one line, then split as a collage blooms in on a peach flush

name: Reel Wall
description: A curved wall of vertical clips turns past in the dark — it eases in from rest, then keeps turning

name: Phone Stack
description: Phone screens playing clips rise out of a blur one after another, each pushing the stack back so the older ones peek out on top

name: Portal Intro
description: A sentence with a picture chip in it leans in until the chip takes the frame, then a title types over the picture and the mark and name arrive

name: Dot Bloom
description: A halftone transition — the outgoing shot washes to cream, breaks into warm drifting dots, and the dots thin out onto the incoming shot

name: Hello Zoom
description: Words flicker in place, one line types on, then the camera dives through its own letters into the next card

name: Spec Sweep
description: A one-line spec slides in word by word while a highlight runs along it and an icon charges up

name: Drop Line
description: Words cut past one card at a time, then the last word sinks out from under the dot of its own i

name: Title Sweep
description: An end title lit by a gradient that travels through the letters, cuts in the dark, and a second title takes over

name: Cut Lockup
description: A logo reveal in hard cuts — huge on grid paper, three cuts down, a push to night where its construction lines draw themselves, then paper wipes up onto the lockup

name: Bloom Lockup
description: A wall of finished work blooms outward from your logo, cuts in tight on it, then bends away through a lens and a flash while the logo rises to take its wordmark

name: Gather Lockup
description: A wall of your work sits under a line of type. The line falls apart word by word, the wall cuts in to a row of four, and each slot swaps its picture and hands over to your mark and wordmark

name: Sky Lockup
description: A one-line promise takes itself apart word by word, the page washes off to a soft sky, and the mark in the middle of the sentence slides over and becomes your logo

name: Search Typing
description: A search field wider than the shot — it comes forward, types across its left half, then pages to its right half

name: Status Cycle
description: A status pill whose label rolls behind a hard clip while its width springs past the target and back, then the field crossfades to a column of chips stepping up from below

name: Type Morph
description: A headline that types itself under a glowing caret, sheds its lead, morphs letter by letter, and ends under a colour flood

name: Orb Swarm
description: A sentence told one beat at a time while glass orbs burst out of it, split into eight and sixteen, wind into a vortex, pay out as a chain and loop around the last words

name: Word Gather
description: A sentence that arrives one word at a time, out of order, and gathers — the first word holds the frame alone, then the rest drop in around it in the accent colour and slide the last of the way home

name: Word Wheel
description: A column of words that spins like a reel and stops on one of them — the lead-in holds the left of the line while the answer rolls into the slot beside it, decelerating over a second and three quarters

name: Brand Wheel
description: A lead word and a wheel of brand pills rolling through where you ship — X, YouTube, LinkedIn, Product Hunt — until a cursor clicks the last one

name: Check Cycle
description: A sentence that finishes itself over and over — the word beside a ticked checkbox rolls up out of a slot, Intros, Demos, Launches, Changelogs, Tutorials, And more — then the line steps back a little and rests

name: Font Shuffle
description: A launch title that decodes out of scrambled glyphs, flashes the accent, then the product name tries on eleven typefaces while the line steps closer

name: Button Press
description: A cursor walks onto a split action button: hover, press, a spinner while it works, then a drawn tick. The deploy beat of every launch video

name: Click Type
description: A prompt composer writes its own placeholder while a cursor flies in and clicks the field, then a hard cut into the field where the prompt types at the caret

name: Capture Reveal
description: A toast counts a screenshot up to 100% over a browser window, the window drops away, "Copied to clipboard." pops and a headline rises out from behind it

name: Channel Thread
description: A work chat filling itself in — faces, a name in bold, a quiet timestamp and messages as plain lines on a dark stage; three dots hold a line until the words arrive, and the transcript scrolls once per arrival and is perfectly still in between

name: Logo Collapse
description: A stack of shots flicked through, collapsing into your mark, and the wordmark landing beside it — each card smaller and held for less time than the last, cutting rather than tweening, until the stack resolves into a logo

name: Card Rail
description: A rail of cards flicked sideways across a tilted plane — pushed three times, each flick leaving at speed and decelerating for over a second into the next, while the plane's foot runs a fifth wider than its head
